verified_points: The find HTTP server registers a /multihash/ endpoint.
The endpoint accepts a base58 or hex encoded multihash and passes the parsed multihash to getIndexes.
The find path queries indexer.Get(multihash); successful results are returned as provider results, including provider identity and addresses resolved from the registry.
An Advertisement signals availability of content to indexers as a list/set of multihashes together with where and how the content is retrievable.
Advertisement includes Provider, Addresses, Entries containing the advertised multihashes, ContextID and Metadata.
Therefore provider/location results for a multihash depend on provider advertisement state that associates that multihash with retrieval information.
Multihash format is varint hash-function code, varint digest size in bytes, then hash-function output.
The SHA-1 example uses function code 0x11 and a 20-byte digest, producing a hex prefix 1114 before the SHA-1 digest.
Thus the deterministic encoding 0x11 0x14 plus the exact 20-byte Git SHA-1 digest is structurally a SHA-1 multihash.
Git documents SHA-1 and SHA-256 object names as distinct object-format identities and maintains an explicit bidirectional mapping when interoperating between formats.

This audit therefore treats the supplied 40-hex SHA-1 commit name only as the exact 20-byte SHA-1 digest being wrapped into a multihash; it does not infer any alternate digest or external content location from the SHA-1 string alone.

verified_claims.claim: IPNI supports namespace-free provider lookup at the API/index-key level when the exact multihash is already indexed.
verified_claims.reason: The find endpoint takes only the multihash key and the indexer returns provider results; no repository namespace is an input to the lookup API.

verified_claims.claim: The exact Git SHA-1 bytes can be deterministically encoded as a SHA-1 multihash by prefixing 0x11 and 0x14.
verified_claims.reason: The multihash primary specification defines code+length+digest and its SHA-1 example uses 0x11 with a 20-byte digest.

verified_claims.claim: Successful IPNI discovery of an arbitrary pre-existing Git commit requires prior index advertisement of the exact derived multihash by a provider; IPNI does not itself establish that target residency merely from the Git SHA-1.
verified_claims.reason: The IPNI advertisement schema makes advertised multihashes and provider retrieval coordinates the source of index availability. The primary sources inspected do not show autonomous crawling or synthesis of a Git-SHA-to-provider mapping.

scope_limits: No live public IPNI endpoint was queried in this slice; this is a primary-source protocol/code verification only.
No evidence was found or claimed that the exact target commit multihash 1114573f2f0a00718109e2cd2fc1c1c9bf2f5a0404de had already been advertised by any provider.
No primary source inspected guarantees that any particular public IPNI endpoint is permanently available with zero finite monthly/trial/paid quota and zero monetary cost.
A fresh advertisement/publication performed to create the mapping would be an external mutation and cannot be counted as satisfying the passive pre-existing-residency leaf.
This result does not establish full scheduled-Chat parity or Phase-1 closure.

phase1_assessment.reason: Primary sources validate the mechanism only after an exact multihash has already been advertised. Exact target pre-existing residency is unproven, and deployed endpoint zero-finite-quota/zero-cost availability is not guaranteed by the inspected primary sources.
